metadata.title: API-pod-loss reliability: loss of one of two API pods

definition.purpose: Decide whether the two-API topology avoids a serving-path outage from the loss of one API pod.
definition.hypothesis: If one of two Ready API pods is deleted while RP-1 runs, the API Service keeps at least one Ready endpoint, and no caller failure episode lasts longer than the preregistered caller bound. This is an expected observation, not an observed one.
gitTransitions: V2-E02C runs at a commit of main whose two desired-state files have the digests of topology.release.desiredStateFiles: the target release.
No commit is made by a run.
setRules: The path-level statement that the two-API topology avoids a single API-pod outage needs all three counted runs to be PASSED. When one is not, the public reliability statement is narrowed to runtime-pod loss.
Three runs give a median and individual values. No confidence interval and no statistical significance are stated.
doesNotEstablish: Node failure, network partition, API overload, or external ingress reliability.
A production SLO or high availability.
Anything about another provider, node, release, or caller workload.
limitations: One provider, one node, one Kubernetes version, one release of each side, one model, and one caller workload. A result is bounded to that execution.

A stream reads a state at intervals of at least 2 s, so a state that lasts less than one interval can be missed. The analysis states an inner and an outer figure for each sampled interval, and neither is the exact time.
The caller instants, the readings, and the events are on three clocks whose differences are not measured.
The runner, the collectors, and the release run on the one node, and the capacity gate does not count the runner.
The API image is built at each run and the build is not byte-reproducible, so each run records the digest it built.

No driver for this experiment exists. The procedure is stated in this record. The change that adds the driver registers a later revision of this record before the first result-bearing run, and that revision pins the driver.
No code holds a declaration of the analysis to definition.analysisDeclaration. The review of each run compares them.
The Service distributes requests over the two API pods. No record shows how many requests each pod served before the fault.
history: This record was written on 2026-10-18, after the qualification and bound chain had run and before any run of V2-E02A, V2-E02B, V2-E02C, V2-E04, or V2-E05. No run of these experiments exists.

Known when it was written: q1-1 QUALIFIED, q2-1 CHARACTERIZED with S = 11,000 ms, q3-1 REFUSED on the environment, q1-2 QUALIFIED, q2-2 CHARACTERIZED with S = 11,000 ms, q3-2 CHARACTERIZED with G = 10,113 ms, and the bound record bounds-r1. The bound values are those of that record, and none was chosen here.

Known when it was written: the two non-result attempts of the Sprint 5 integration validation. integration-2 deleted one API pod by name while an RP-1 runner ran on this provider, and its figures were published. It is not a run of any of these experiments.

Known when it was written: on 2026-10-04 three runs of the Application procedure each saw one manual change to a replica count reverted, and the Deployment declared its committed value again within 2 to 4 s. Those were not experiment runs and no bound was compared.
executionGate: No result-bearing run starts until this record is merged into main and registered. A run executes at a merged commit that holds the record with its registered digest, and its manifest names the record and that commit.
No run is authorized by this record alone. A run needs the explicit authorization of the repository owner for the cluster mutations and, where the procedure names them, the commits to main.

A change after this record merges that alters the caller profile, the topology, the fault, a measurement, a window, a bound, an outcome rule, an exclusion reason, an abort condition, the cleanup, or a criterion is material. It is a later revision of this record, merged before any run under it.

A change that adds the driver, or that moves a pinned input, is a later revision that classifies each moved input as material or not, with the reason. The run refuses to start while python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes lists a file that no merged revision classifies.
No criterion, bound, window, or exclusion reason is changed after the evidence of a run is read. A revision written after a run states the runs it was written after.
preparation: P1. Check out a commit of main that holds this record with the content digest that the freeze registry pins, with a clean working tree. That commit is the executing revision. python -m tools.experiment_freeze --check, python -m tools.experiment_preregistration --check, python -m tools.environment_qualification --check, and python -m tools.experiment_bounds --check each pass, and python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes for this record lists no file, or only files that a merged later revision of this record classifies. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P2. Read the remote main as the desired revision. The chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing revision equal those of the desired revision. The two files at topology.desiredStatePath of the desired revision have the content digests that topology.release.desiredStateFiles states. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P3. Run the target check of the operating procedures. It selects the docker-desktop provider and refuses every other. The cluster holds no release of the release key and no delivery controller. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P4. Read capacity with scripts/environment/capacity-preflight.sh before the Application is applied. The gate accepts the reading, and its stable environment identity has the environmentSha256 of environmentIdentity. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P5. Prepare the release as the qualification q1-2 did: apply the Terraform prerequisite layer with scripts/environment/terraform-prerequisites.sh, fill the model cache claim from the local seed image of scripts/environment/model-seed-image.sh through one preparation Helm release that is uninstalled before the Application is applied, install the delivery controller with scripts/environment/argocd-bootstrap.sh, build the API image at the executing revision with scripts/environment/api-image.sh, and apply the Application with scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh apply and the digest of that image. A step that fails ends the run as REFUSED, and nothing is changed to fit.

P6. Wait at most 1,800 s for the topology: both Deployments report the replica counts of topology as readyReplicas, both Services report as many Ready endpoints, and the Application reports Synced and Healthy at the desired revision. scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh verify finds the live Application and project equal to the committed manifests. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

P7. Resolve the provenance of the release key at the desired revision with tools/desired_state_provenance. Its release identifier is topology.release.releaseId. Each runtime pod reports, in its model verification log, the model file SHA-256 of topology.model. Otherwise the run is REFUSED.

callerRun.endState: duration: a run whose record ends in another end state does not cover its window and is INCONCLUSIVE
callerRun.collect: scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh collect, after the Job ends, and cleanup after that
callerRun.independence: The caller record is the reference for every caller figure. No stream, readiness state, endpoint count, replica count, sync state, health state, or scrape state changes a caller figure.

collection.order: Open the operator event log with tools/experiment_events open, start the timeline collector and then the telemetry collector, wait 30 s, and start the runner. Each collector runs until it has taken its samples.
collection.timeline: scripts/environment/experiment-timeline.sh --experiment <experiment> --run <run> --samples 900 --interval 2: the streams endpoints, pods, deployments, and argo
collection.telemetry: scripts/environment/experiment-telemetry.sh --experiment <experiment> --run <run> --samples 120 --interval 15: the streams telemetry and resources, from the registered query set experiment-run-queries-r1. A query with no series is stated as no-series and is not read as zero
collection.events: tools/experiment_events record for each event of the procedure, by the control process or the operator, and tools/experiment_events close after the window ends
collection.coverage: The pauses alone of each collector cover the runner's duration and 60 s more, whatever each read lasts.

definition.stablePreFaultWindow: The stable pre-fault window holds at a check when the caller record that the runner has written so far, read with kubectl logs from its pod, holds at least 10 successful requests that completed in the 60 s before the check, the last completed request succeeded, and both Deployments report the replica counts of topology as readyReplicas. The control checks at 150 s after the runner pod started, and every 30 s after that, until 600 s after it started. The fault is injected at the first check at which the window holds. When it does not hold at 600 s, no fault is injected, the runner is removed, and the run is REFUSED.
faultProcedure: F1. At the check at which the stable pre-fault window holds, read the API pods of the release and select the fault target by the rule of fault.target. Record its name and UID, and the name and UID of every other pod of the release.
F2. Record the event fault-injection-started with the code delete-api-pod and the subject pod/<name>, with tools/experiment_events record, immediately before the command.
F3. Run kubectl delete pod <name> --namespace inferops-release --wait=false once. The default grace period applies.
F4. Record the event fault-injection-finished with the same code and subject immediately after the command returns. Keep the command and its output in commands.txt and transcript.txt.
definition.observation: After the fault, the control issues no mutating command and observes. The observation limit is 600 s after the fault-injection-finished event. The runner runs to its duration, and the collectors run to their samples. A stabilized recovery that the analysis states after the observation limit is not a recovery inside it.
definition.postRecoveryWindow: When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.

window.from: The recordedAt instant of the fault-injection-started event, less 60,000 ms
window.to: The recordedAt instant of the fault-injection-finished event, plus 720,000 ms
window.clocks: A caller instant is on the clock of the runner pod. A reading is on the clock of the collecting host, and an event on the clock of the recording host. The difference between the clocks is not measured, and no order of two instants of two clocks that are less than one second apart is stated.

analysisDeclaration.experimentId: the experiment identifier of this record
analysisDeclaration.window: the window of definition.window, to one millisecond

expected.desiredRevision: the desired revision that P2 read

analysisDeclaration.rule: The declaration of a run is written from this rule before its evidence is read, with each topology member replaced by its value. It is stored in the run directory, and tools/analysis_replay bind embeds it in the run analysis. No code holds a declaration to this rule: the review of the run compares them.

measurements: The caller figures of the run analysis: requests completed, successful, and failed in the window; each failure episode, and callerFailureEpisodeMs; maxSuccessGap; the first caller impact; and the stabilized recovery, with requestsFailedSinceFault and the time from each fault instant.

From the caller record, on the result page: requests started and completed, the count of each HTTP status and of each canonical error code and condition, the nearest-rank p50, p90, and p99 and the minimum and maximum of the latency of the successful requests, the longest run of failed completions with no success between them, and the time from the fault-injection-finished event to the first successful completion after the first failure.
The zero-Ready-endpoint intervals of both tiers, with the inner and the outer figure of each, from the endpoints stream.
The state of each API pod and runtime pod at each reading: its UID, template hash, revision, phase, Ready condition, restart counts, creation instant, and deletion timestamp.
The Deployment counts of both tiers at each reading: generation, observedGeneration, specReplicas, replicas, updatedReplicas, readyReplicas, availableReplicas, and unavailableReplicas.
The Application at each reading: the followed and the resolved revision, the sync state, the health state, and the last operation. It is recorded, and it is not a caller conclusion.
The telemetry and resource streams of the registered query set, with each no-series answer kept as no-series.
For each replacement pod: the time from its creation to its first Ready condition, from its createdAt and readyTransitionAt, to one second.
Each signal of the declaration: its detection lag, its false-healthy time, and its false-unavailable time.
outcomeRules: REFUSED: a precondition did not hold, and no fault was injected.
ABORTED: the run started and crossed an abort condition. The run-aborted event records the condition, and the cleanup is recorded.
INCONCLUSIVE: no abort condition was crossed, and a criterion of kind validity did not hold.
FAILED: every criterion of kind validity held, and a criterion of kind pass did not.

A run has exactly one state. The result page states each criterion, its kind, the evidence it was judged from, and the verdict. The run analysis states the figures, and the result page states the state.
definition.repetitionRule: 3 counted runs. A run is counted when its state is PASSED or FAILED. A counted run is never repeated, replaced, or left out of an aggregate. A run that is REFUSED, INCONCLUSIVE, or ABORTED for a registered exclusion reason is kept, and the next run takes the next identifier. At most 6 runs start under one revision. When fewer than 3 runs are counted after 6, the set is INCONCLUSIVE, and a further run needs a later revision of this record. Each run begins with the preparation P1 to P7 and ends with the cleanup.

parts.title: API-pod-loss reliability: loss of one of two API pods
parts.question: With two API replicas and two runtime replicas, in the environment of q1-2, does the API Service keep a Ready endpoint, and does every caller failure episode stay within the caller bound, when one API pod is deleted while RP-1 runs?

value.definition: This record states the purpose, the procedure, the measurements, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them, or to a pinned input, is a later revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file in materialScope is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that adds it, so the pins freeze the files and not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each run executes at a merged commit of main that holds this record with its registered digest, with a clean working tree. The manifest names that commit as executingRevision.

value.selection: q1-2 is the selected environment of the reliability experiments. It is QUALIFIED under revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, at the commit ed892a4eac2ee505996f53b6d3e0da31b8e4e204, on the docker-desktop provider with one node. Its stable environment identity states the provider, the server version, the node with its kubelet version and the CPU and the pods that it allocates, and the CPU count of the container engine. It states no memory figure: memory is a capacity fact that the capacity gate decides on each reading.
value.perRun: Before the release is applied, each run reads capacity with scripts/environment/capacity-preflight.sh. The gate must accept the reading, and the stable environment identity of the reading must have the environmentSha256 above. Otherwise the run is REFUSED, and nothing is changed to fit: no replica count, request, limit, or bound.
value.notAnotherEnvironment: A run on another provider, on another node, or with another stable identity is not a run of this record. No cloud resource is used, and a run that uses one is not a run of this record.

value.runner: tools/reliability_runner/incluster.py in a Job of the release namespace, started by scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh. The runner sends the fixed RP-1 request through the API Service, never to a named pod.
value.unchangedFrom: The profile that the qualification q1-2 and the characterizations q2-2 and q3-2 ran. The record of q1-2 states the same content digest.

delivery.controller: Argo CD v3.5.3, installed by scripts/environment/argocd-bootstrap.sh from the pinned core install manifest
delivery.apiImageDigest: The API image is built at the executing commit by scripts/environment/api-image.sh and given to the Application as the one Helm parameter api.image.digest by scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh. The build is not byte-reproducible, so each run records the digest it built.

value.apiDisruptionBudget: The chart renders one PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable 1 for the API tier.
value.runtimeDisruptionBudget: The chart renders one PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable 1 for the runtime tier.
value.statement: Two API replicas and two serving runtime replicas: the desired-state release that the qualification q1-2 qualified, delivered by the Application from the desired-state path at the remote main.

value.target: The Ready API pod of the release whose name is first in ascending order at the fault check.
value.mechanism: kubectl delete pod <name> --namespace inferops-release --wait=false, once, with the default grace period, while the RP-1 runner is active. The Deployment controller replaces the pod.
value.notChanged: No Service, runtime pod, node, persistent volume claim, Deployment, or delivery controller object is deleted or changed.
value.timestamp: The control process that issues the command records fault-injection-started immediately before it and fault-injection-finished immediately after it. fault-injection-started is the authoritative fault instant.

value.statement: The control deleted exactly the pod that the rule of fault.target selected (the first Ready API pod by name), once, by name: commands.txt holds one delete command, the fault-injection-started event names that pod, and a pods reading after the event shows that UID with a deletion timestamp or absent. No other pod of the release has a deletion timestamp before the end of the observation, except a pod that the Deployment controller removes.

The endpoints stream is accepted by its reader, states a Ready endpoint count of both tiers in its first and its last reading inside the window, and has at most 10 s between two consecutive readings with a count inside the window.

The caller record is accepted by its reader with the plan, in the mode in-cluster, with the API Service as its target and the end state duration. It covers the window, and at least one request completes inside the window after the fault-injection-finished event.

Either a pod of the tier of the fault with a UID that no pod had before the fault is Ready in a pods reading and the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, or the observation limit is reached. The result page states which.

When the analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, at least 10 successful requests complete after the stabilizedAt instant inside the window, and the last of them completes at least 60 s after it.

Every file that evidencePaths lists is present and named by the manifest, the operator event log is closed, python -m tools.experiment_evidence check accepts the run directory, and python -m tools.analysis_replay verify reproduces its run analysis.

The API Service never has fewer than 1 Ready endpoint after the fault: no endpoints reading that starts at or after the fault-injection-started event and finishes inside the window states an API Ready count of 0, and the analysis states no zero-Ready-endpoint interval of the API tier after that event.

The runtime Service has 2 Ready endpoints in every endpoints reading inside the window. A runtime pod that restarts or is replaced inside the window makes the run INCONCLUSIVE for the reason unrelated-failure, and not PASSED or FAILED.

No caller failure episode exceeds caller_total_unavailability_bound_ms, 20,226 ms: the analysis states callerFailureEpisodeMs with a value of at most 20,226 ms. An open episode is not within the bound.
The deleted API pod is replaced under the Deployment controller: an API pod with a new UID, of the template hash that the API pods had before the fault, is Ready inside the observation limit.
The analysis states a stabilized recovery inside the observation limit, with readyReplicas 2 and 2 and two Ready runtime endpoints, and the operator event log holds no manual-action event.

value.role: These are preregistered, shared experiment-reference bounds. tools/experiment_bounds derived them from the characterizations q2-2 and q3-2. Both ran on the qualified target release, b5457f49092c578496738973a8786a95428517e7ddf755303b4f6842dcb8c9db, with two API replicas and two runtime replicas, in the environment of q1-2. They are not bounds of another release. No characterization of the single-runtime baseline release exists, and none is attributed to it. They are experiment bounds, not service levels, availability targets, or production thresholds.

value: The target check verifies a provider other than docker-desktop, or a command reaches another cluster than the one that it verified.
The control or a person changes an object or a field other than the declared fault target, or injects the fault twice.
The runner pod is deleted, evicted, or restarted, or its Job fails, before the window ends, so the caller stream is lost.
The delivery controller reports a resolved revision that is not a commit that the procedure names.
The model cache claim or its volume is deleted, or a runtime pod reports a model file SHA-256 other than that of topology.model.
The node is not Ready, or the Kubernetes API does not answer, for more than 60 s.
A tracked file of the checkout of the run changes while the run executes.
A namespace or a custom resource definition appears or disappears that the preparation does not create.
A cleanup step cannot be executed without deleting an object that the run did not create.
abortConditions.note: An abort is recorded with the event run-aborted and the code of the condition. The run is kept as ABORTED, and its cleanup is recorded. Abort is an outcome, not something to repeat away.

value: C1. After the window ends and the runner Job has ended: collect the caller record with scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh collect, then remove the run's objects with its cleanup action, and read the objects that carry the run's label.
C2. After the collectors have taken their samples: close the operator event log, and write the streams with tools/experiment_timeline stream and tools/experiment_telemetry stream.

C3. Verify the desired state before removal: scripts/environment/argocd-application.sh verify finds the live Application and project equal to the committed manifests, both Deployments report spec.replicas and readyReplicas of topology, and the Application reports Synced at the desired revision. A difference is recorded as remaining drift.

C4. Remove the Application, the delivery controller, and the prerequisite layer as the phase down of the qualification did, and compare the namespaces and the custom resource definitions with those read before P5.
C5. Keep the collections and the runner directory under .artifacts/ until the run directory is assembled, and preserve the evidence before any ephemeral telemetry is removed.

intendedEvidenceLevel.note: Runtime: a real cluster, the delivery controller, the real runtime, and the real model, on one provider and one node. Bounded to the environment that this record names, and not representative. A C3 candidate needs a separate admission and preregistration.

reasons.reason: A precondition of the run did not hold, and no fault was injected.
The stable pre-fault window did not hold by 600 s after the runner pod started, and no fault was injected.
The fault command ran and did not produce the declared condition.
A stream that a criterion reads was refused by its reader, or has more than 10 s between two consecutive readings with a value inside the window.
The caller record was refused by its reader, does not cover the window, or does not hold the post-recovery window after a stabilized recovery.
A container of a pod that the fault did not target restarted, or a pod that the fault did not target was replaced, inside the window.
A file of the evidence paths is absent, the layout check refuses the run directory, or the run analysis is not reproduced.
The run crossed an abort condition of the freeze record, and the run-aborted event records which.
